762.t: Closing thoughts on Bunk's band and George Lewis
762.s: He prefers jazz to better money, praises George Lewis's band as authentic, and wishes to reunite it.
762.q: I just like to add that I like the jazz. When I went to New York with Bunk's band, Bill, I could have made more money playing with Smiling Joe. But I like the jazz so much that I'd rather be with them. And right now, Bill, I think that George Lewis who has the band, has one of the greatest…

743.t: Best experience now, and past stints with Spanier, Condon and Hackett
743.s: Gordon is happiest playing with Grosz, Robinson, Ingham and Smith and The Orphan Newsboys, after short earlier stints with Spanier, Condon, Hackett and McPartland.
743.q: Well what I’m doing now is what I really enjoy. I’ve never enjoyed anything so much because I’m getting a chance to play with musicians that are great New York musicians, and as I say again, a lot of them are here today: Scott Robinson, Marty Grosz, Keith Ingham, Hal Smith. Just in the last ten or…

954.s: Rowe and LaLama agree on what horns and rhythm sections behind James Brown teach; Rowe then asks which big band leader he enjoyed most.
954.q: Yeah. And the rhythm section, the feeling. The feeling. James Brown — I still love it. I mean to me that’s how good it is. When I put it on now, after all I’ve been through in a musical sense, I still enjoy it as much. So to me that’s true art. That might not be in the books as art, but to me it…

856.t: Big band experience with Illinois Jacquet and Mel Lewis
856.s: He enjoys all kinds of playing and valued working in the Jacquet and Mel Lewis bands and Thad Jones's music.
856.q: Yeah. I enjoy every kind of playing. I don’t have any particular love of big bands as a lot of people do, nor do I despise it. But playing with a great band, I mean you mentioned Illinois Jacquet and at the time I was in the band it was a really great band and a wonderful learning experience. And…

217.t: Highlight: Haggart and Lawson band and Emporium of Jazz tape
217.s: He loved the Haggart-Lawson band and recalls a tape from the Emporium of Jazz near Minneapolis.
217.q: But we had a great band. And a guy sent me a tape, a cassette, from Minneapolis. We played in a place, oh this goes back to the early ‘70s. And we played a place outside of Minneapolis, called the Emporium of Jazz. And the band was Benny Morton on trombone, Yank Lawson, Billy Butterfield, Bud…

167.t: Which groups he enjoyed most and the Ink Spots
167.s: The Spirits were his favorite; Louis Jordan, Ink Spots, Edgar Hayes and others were jobs, and he never recorded with the Ink Spots.
167.q: [Deak.] Yeah. I wondered why they didn't like they did. stay together, but they didn't. It's a shame. Most of them's gone now.

18.s: He remembers no bad band but enjoyed Luis Russell most for fun and music.
18.q: Yeah, they're all good. I don't remember nothing bad about no band I played with, no band. Every band I played with, I enjoyed myself.

388.t: The Lawson-Haggart band and its 30 albums
388.s: Leeman calls the Yank Lawson-Bob Haggart band a mutual admiration society where he never had a bad night across nearly thirty albums.
388.q: And that was another great -- which I did after Eddie Condon's -- the feeling inside, we did almost 30 or 31 albums with the Lawson-Haggard band, and still working on the outside, and it was nothing but a mutual admiration society. It was terrible on our record dates because we'd sit around like a…

19.t: A show-business band after Eckstine: shuffle rhythm and chartreuse uniforms
19.s: Jordan's music was mostly vocals and shows, a contrast to the Eckstine band, but he finds it enjoyable with good musicians.
19.ch: Washington clubs, Louis Jordan and Sarah Vaughan, 1949-54
19.q: Altogether, it was a very nice and different kind of experience, because being in a band like that was quite different than anything that I had been in. First of all, the kind of stuff that Louis Jordan was doing, after coming out of a band like the Eckstine band, with Charlie Parker and people…

13.t: Favorite bands: Hines, Lefty Bates and Joe Kelly
13.q: Well, my real favorite band, big band, was the Earl Fatha Hines. And my little band was Lefty Bates band, until I joined Joe Kelly. And after John Board started with Joe Kelly, then we really got together on, you know, different arrangements, and suggestions from Johnny Board. He really brought the…
